data.narrative:
Ultra Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Miller Schwartz, Max Friefeld, Chetan Parthiban, and Oliver Ortlieb, having raised $3M+. The valuation benchmark draws from a sector universe of 9 private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $3M total raised as a proxy for base valuation, a 2.5x step-up multiplier—consistent with typical Seed-to-next-stage progression in frontier tech—yields an implied valuation of $8M. This method is appropriate given the early stage and capital-efficient path typical of robotics infrastructure plays.

Peer-median analysis is not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer cohort; while 10 same-sector robotics peers exist, none meet simultaneous filters for stage, adjacency, and valuation tier to form a reliable median. This analysis therefore relies on the single methodological signal available.

The triangulated range is $6M (low) to $9M (high), with a median of $8M. This valuation reflects early-stage risk and limited revenue visibility typical at Seed. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation versus the broader peer set, path to next institutional round, and margin profile once manufacturing scales. Additional data on comparable rounds in the peer set would materially improve confidence in this range.
